result.process_summary: Both gold prospecting and data mining involve exploring a vast domain (mountains or datasets), first surveying to locate promising regions, then applying specialized tools (prospecting equipment or algorithms) to separate valuable material (gold nuggets or insights) from the bulk (rock or regular data). The process includes pattern recognition to guide extraction, detection of unexpected valuable items (anomalies), and continual refinement of techniques based on experience.
potential_breaks: Physical extraction constraints in gold prospecting differ from computational extraction in data mining.
Gold prospecting often relies on a single pass over terrain, whereas data mining may be iterative with feedback loops.
The tangible value of gold does not map directly to the abstract value of data insights.
Geological randomness in prospecting is not identical to the statistical properties of data.
